overall: The AG found the Board failed to timely approve the September 11, 2023 minutes, approving them at the fourth meeting after, and that the violation was intentional. No civil penalty was recommended; immediate and future compliance was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely approve the minutes of its September 11, 2023 meeting, and urged that the violation was intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board failed to timely approve the minutes of the meeting held on September 11, 2023.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, and a caution that a future intentional violation may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and caution the Board that a future finding of an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
